# System overview

Every box is clickable: it opens that part's section below, with a smaller diagram of what it works with. Use **Full window** to explore the diagrams at full size; **Esc** closes it.

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/system.svg" aria-label="VizDOM system overview" style="aspect-ratio:1160/850"></object></div></div>

On one machine everything in the engine runs **inside your test process**; nothing has to be started. The services in the dashed band are the same parts, moved to another machine when you want one GPU host to serve many test runners, or when the application runs somewhere else.

## Where you work

### Robot Framework library { #c-rf }

*Write GUI tests in Robot Framework against what VizDOM sees on the screen.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/rf.svg" aria-label="Robot Framework library: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/276"></object></div></div>

`VisualGuiLibrary` gives a Robot suite keywords that work on the Visual DOM:
`Connect`, `Dump Visual DOM`, `Click Visual`, `Type Text Visual`,
`Visual Should Exist`, `Wait Until Visual Appears`, `Verify Element Value`,
`Bring App To Front` and more.

```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    VisualGuiLibrary

*** Test Cases ***
Save The Document
    Connect              vizdom.config.json
    Bring App To Front   Notepad
    Dump Visual DOM
    Click Visual         text=Save || desc="save button"
```

The suite parses a screen once (`Dump Visual DOM`); every click and check after
that is resolved against that DOM until the layout changes. When a keyword fails,
the library saves a screenshot of the application window.

**Install:** `pip install "vizdom[robot]"`, or use the Python that comes with the
VizDOM Studio installer.

**More:** [Using as a Client](USAGE.md)

### VizDOM Studio { #c-studio }

*Look at an application the way VizDOM does, and build locators by hand.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/studio.svg" aria-label="VizDOM Studio: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/492"></object></div></div>

| Area | What you do there |
|---|---|
| **Capture & Analyze** (F5) | Pick a window; Studio hides itself, captures it and builds its Visual DOM |
| **Inspect** | Element list, zoomable canvas coloured by element type, the locators of each element |
| **Locator Lab** | Type a locator and see live what it matches: one match is green, an ambiguous one amber |
| **Try click** | Capture again, resolve the locator as a test would, click through the actuator |
| **Export** (Ctrl E) | Write a Robot Framework `.resource` with the chosen elements |
| **Services** (Ctrl 3) | Start, stop and watch the detector, capture and actuator services |
| **Settings** (Ctrl ,) | Edit the session config, checked by VizDOM itself |

The installer brings its own Python with everything VizDOM needs. Your config,
sessions and plugins are kept in `Documents\VizDOM`.

**More:** [README: VizDOM Studio](https://github.com/milanac030988/vizdom/tree/HEAD/tools/vizdom_studio)

### Python API & CLI { #c-python }

*Build a Visual DOM from your own code, a script or another test framework.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/python.svg" aria-label="Python API &amp; CLI: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/204"></object></div></div>

```python
from visual_dom import connect

session = connect("vizdom.config.json")   # or connect() for the defaults
dom = session.analyze("screenshot.png")   # -> Visual DOM (dict)
```

The same session object captures the screen and drives the actuator, so any test
framework can use VizDOM, not only Robot Framework.

**More:** [Using as a Client](USAGE.md) · [Commands](COMMANDS.md)

## The VizDOM engine

### Session config { #c-config }

*One JSON file chooses the detector, OCR, capture, input and grounding, for every entry point.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/config.svg" aria-label="Session config: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/348"></object></div></div>

```bash
python -m visual_dom.config --init vizdom.config.json   # annotated template
```

| Section | Chooses |
|---|---|
| `detector` | `uied` (CPU), `omniparser`, `modular`, `yolo`, or `grpc` for the detector service |
| `ocr` | `easyocr`, `tesseract`, `paddleocr`, or `none` |
| `capture` | `windows`, `linux`, `android`, `camera`, `grpc`, or a plugin; the window to target |
| `actuator` | `desktop`, `android`, `grpc`, or a plugin |
| `grounding` | the `desc=` tiers: `lexical`, `slm`, `vlm`, and the models behind them |

Moving a part to another machine is a change in this file only, e.g.
`"detector": {"backend": "grpc", "grpc_target": "gpu-host:50051"}`.

**More:** [Configuration & Sessions](CONFIGURATION.md)

### Capture { #c-capture }

*Takes the screenshot: the whole screen, or only the window of the application under test.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/capture.svg" aria-label="Capture: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/276"></object></div></div>

Built-in sources: `windows`, `linux` (X11), `android` (adb) and `camera` (a
physical screen photographed and rectified). With `capture.window_title` and
`capture.window_scope` it captures only the application under test, raised to the
front first, so the DOM does not describe whatever window happens to be on top.

Set `capture.strategy` to `grpc` to take the screenshot on another machine through
the [capture service](#c-capsvc).

**More:** [Configuration: capture](CONFIGURATION.md) · [Writing Plugins](PLUGINS.md)

### Detection pipeline { #c-pipeline }

*Turns the screenshot into elements: boxes, text, types and a containment tree.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/pipeline.svg" aria-label="Detection pipeline: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/420"></object></div></div>

1. **Detect** the elements with the configured backend: UIED (CPU, no weights),
   OmniParser or the modular detector (GPU recommended), or YOLO.
2. **Read text** with EasyOCR, Tesseract or PaddleOCR, and read glyph keys
   (`+ − × ÷ =`) that have no text.
3. **Merge** duplicates and over-split boxes, and sort in reading order.
4. **Build the hierarchy** by containment, and attach labels to inputs.

With `detector.backend = grpc` the detection step runs on the
[detector service](#c-detsvc), e.g. on a GPU host.

**More:** [CV Pipeline](PIPELINE.md) · [OmniParser Setup](omniparser-setup.md)

### Visual DOM { #c-dom }

*The result: every element with its role, text, label, flags and ready-made locators.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/dom.svg" aria-label="Visual DOM: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/190"></object></div></div>

Each element has its bounds, role, text, label, interaction flags (clickable,
editable, scrollable), its parent in the hierarchy and locator suggestions. Every
analysis is saved as a session folder:

```
output/sessions/<timestamp>/
    screenshot.png       the captured screen
    dom_result.json      the Visual DOM
    session_info.json    where the screenshot came from
```

Studio and the Viewer open the same folders.

**More:** [Configuration & Sessions](CONFIGURATION.md)

### Locator resolver { #c-locator }

*Finds the one element a locator means, or fails the step.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/locator.svg" aria-label="Locator resolver: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/348"></object></div></div>

| Locator | Matches |
|---|---|
| `text=Save`, `hint=Email`, `role=button`, `id=E12` | by what the element says or is |
| `right_of="Name"`, `below="Title"`, `within="Dialog"` | by position relative to another element |
| `desc="save button"` | by a plain-language description |
| <code>text=Save &#124;&#124; desc="save button"</code> | the first alternative that resolves wins |

A locator must resolve to **exactly one** element; none or several fails the step,
so an absent element is never reported as found. `desc=` is resolved in tiers:
`lexical` (no model) first; what it cannot settle goes to a vision model (`vlm`,
the default, GPU) or a small language model (`slm`, CPU) through
[Ollama](#c-ollama).

**More:** [Using as a Client: locators](USAGE.md)

### Plugins { #c-plugins }

*Add a capture source or an input device without changing VizDOM.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/plugins.svg" aria-label="Plugins: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/204"></object></div></div>

Drop a Python file into `plugins/capture/` or `plugins/actuator/` (Studio:
`Documents\VizDOM\plugins\…`), or point `VIZDOM_CAPTURE_PLUGINS` /
`VIZDOM_ACTUATOR_PLUGINS` at a folder. The plugin is then selectable by name in
the config, like a built-in one: a camera, a capture card, a robot arm.

**More:** [Writing Plugins](PLUGINS.md)

### Actuator { #c-actuator }

*Delivers the click, the keystrokes and the scroll to the application.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/actuator.svg" aria-label="Actuator: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/276"></object></div></div>

Built-in: `desktop` (mouse and keyboard on Windows and Linux) and `android`
(adb input). Before input it can raise the application under test, so the click
reaches it and not the window on top (`actuator.window_title`, or the keyword
`Bring App To Front`).

Set `actuator.strategy` to `grpc` to deliver the input on another machine through
the [actuator service](#c-actsvc).

**More:** [Configuration: actuator](CONFIGURATION.md)

## Optional services

### Capture service { #c-capsvc }

*Takes the screenshot on the machine that shows the application.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/capsvc.svg" aria-label="Capture service: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/204"></object></div></div>

```bash
vizdom-capture --strategy windows --port 50053
```

Client side: `"capture": {"strategy": "grpc", "target": "sut-host:50053"}`.

**More:** [Using as a Client: services](USAGE.md)

### Detector service { #c-detsvc }

*Runs the detector on a GPU host, one warm model for every test runner.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/detsvc.svg" aria-label="Detector service: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/204"></object></div></div>

```bash
# source checkout (see OmniParser Setup)
uv pip install -e ".[robot,omniparser]"
python scripts/setup_omniparser.py           # model weights, once
vizdom-detector --backend omniparser --port 50051
```

Client side: `"detector": {"backend": "grpc", "grpc_target": "gpu-host:50051"}`.
`--backend uied` runs on a CPU and needs no weights.

**More:** [OmniParser Setup](omniparser-setup.md) · [Using as a Client: services](USAGE.md)

### Language model { #c-ollama }

*Resolves the descriptions the lexical tier cannot, e.g. a paraphrase.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/ollama.svg" aria-label="Language model: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/190"></object></div></div>

Needed for the model tiers of `desc=`. The default chain is `lexical` (no model)
then `vlm`, a 7B vision model that wants a GPU; on a machine without one, use
`slm`, a 3B text model that runs on a CPU.

```bash
ollama pull qwen2.5vl:7b      # vlm tier (default), GPU recommended
ollama pull qwen2.5:3b        # slm tier, runs on a CPU
```

Default: `"grounding": {"tiers": ["lexical", "vlm"], "host": "http://gpu-host:11434"}`;
CPU only: `"tiers": ["lexical", "slm"]`. `text=`, `role=` and the other locators
need no model at all.

**More:** [Configuration: grounding](CONFIGURATION.md)

### Actuator service { #c-actsvc }

*Delivers clicks and keystrokes on the machine that runs the application.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/actsvc.svg" aria-label="Actuator service: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/204"></object></div></div>

```bash
vizdom-actuator --strategy desktop --port 50054
```

Client side: `"actuator": {"strategy": "grpc", "target": "sut-host:50054"}`.

!!! warning "Trusted networks only"
    The services have no TLS and no authentication and listen on every network
    interface. The actuator executes the clicks and keystrokes it receives.

**More:** [Using as a Client: services](USAGE.md)

## The application under test

### Application under test { #c-aut }

*Any application with a screen: desktop, embedded HMI, Android, or a screen seen through a camera.*

<div class="vz-fig"><div class="vz-scroll"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="../overview/components/aut.svg" aria-label="Application under test: what it works with" style="aspect-ratio:1320/348"></object></div></div>

VizDOM needs nothing inside the application: no test build, no injected agent,
no accessibility API. It sees the pixels and sends input like a user, so the
same suite works on custom-rendered Qt/OpenGL interfaces, industrial HMIs and
remote desktops.
